motivation: To solve exterior Helmholtz scattering problems without truncation errors from artificial boundaries, by incorporating infinity as a computational boundary.
method: A hyperboloidal compactification transforms the unbounded domain into a bounded one, and an H1-conforming finite-element formulation with a boundary mass term is derived.
result: The method yields accurate far-field patterns and compares favorably with PML-based discretizations in 2D and 3D benchmarks.
conclusion: The null-infinity-layer approach provides an effective alternative to PML for Helmholtz scattering, with potential extensions to time-dependent problems.

title: A Bargmann Transform For Translation Invariant Operators On Weighted Bergman Spaces Of The Complex Half-plane
authors: Raul Quiroga-Barranco
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let us denote with [MATH] ([MATH]) a weighted Bergman space over the right half-plane [MATH], which admits a unitary representation of [MATH] given by the (imaginary) translations of [MATH]. We study the von Neumann algebra [MATH] of bounded translation invariant operators. We prove that every element of [MATH] is a Toeplit operator [MATH] for some translation invariant operator [MATH] of the ambient [MATH]-space of [MATH]. Furthermore, we prove that this can be achieved through a commutative von Neumann algebra [MATH] that yields an assignment [MATH] that turns out to be a [MATH]-isomorphism of [MATH]-algebras. Our main tool is a Bargmann transform [MATH] for which we establish several operator and representation theoretic properties. We also describe the translation invariant subspaces of [MATH] and obtain formulas for the diagonalizing spectral functions for translation invariant Toeplitz operators whose symbols are translation invariant operators. The latter generalize previously known results for function symbols.
tldr: This paper studies translation invariant operators on weighted Bergman spaces over the complex half-plane using a Bargmann transform, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The work is motivated by functional analysis and operator theory, specifically the structure of von Neumann algebras generated by translation invariant operators.
method: The authors introduce a Bargmann transform and use it to establish a *-isomorphism between the von Neumann algebra of translation invariant operators and a commutative von Neumann algebra of Toeplitz operators.
result: Every translation invariant operator on the weighted Bergman space is shown to be a Toeplitz operator with a translation invariant symbol, and the translation invariant subspaces are described.
conclusion: The paper provides a complete algebraic and spectral characterization of translation invariant operators on these spaces, generalizing known results for function symbols.

title: Notes On Q-normed Spaces In Constructive Analysis
authors: Douglas S. Bridges
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25236v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: What we call q-normed (linear) spaces were introduced (under the name pseudonormed spaces) into constructive analysis by D.L. Johns as a means of handling spaces, such as L-infinity, in which not all elements are constructively normable. We prove a number of q-normed-space analogues/generalisations of standard theorems in the constructive analysis of normed linear spaces, and give examples showing that analogues of two of those theorems are essentially nonconstructive.
tldr: This paper studies q-normed spaces in constructive analysis, proving analogues of standard theorems and showing nonconstructive limitations.
motivation: To extend constructive analysis to spaces like L-infinity where not all elements are constructively normable, using q-normed spaces introduced by D.L. Johns.
method: The paper proves q-normed-space analogues of standard theorems in constructive analysis of normed linear spaces, and provides examples demonstrating nonconstructivity of certain analogues.
result: Several analogues/generalizations of standard theorems are established, while two theorems are shown to be essentially nonconstructive.
conclusion: Q-normed spaces provide a useful framework for constructive analysis of spaces with non-normable elements, but some classical results do not have constructive analogues.

title: Formalization Of Line Search Methods By Lean
authors: Kenneth W. Shum Yiyang Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a formalization of line search methods in the Lean 4 theorem prover. Our goal is to advance machine verification of nonlinear optimization theory by translating standard textbook definitions and convergence arguments into rigorous Lean code. We formalize fundamental notions related to gradient descent and descent directions, adaptive step-size selection via backtracking line search, and several classical line search criteria, including the Armijo, Goldstein, and Wolfe conditions, as well as nonmonotone variants. We further formalize a key convergence result, namely the Zoutendijk theorem, which plays a central role in the global convergence analysis of gradient-based iterative methods. By providing machine-checkable definitions and proofs for line search theory, this work complements existing formalizations of first-order optimization methods and establishes a foundation for the verified development of more advanced algorithms in nonlinear programming.
tldr: This paper formalizes line search methods for nonlinear optimization in the Lean 4 theorem prover.
motivation: To advance machine verification of nonlinear optimization theory by providing rigorous, machine-checkable proofs.
method: Translates standard textbook definitions and convergence arguments into Lean 4 code, formalizing gradient descent, backtracking line search, Armijo/Goldstein/Wolfe conditions, and the Zoutendijk theorem.
result: A formalization of key line search concepts and a convergence theorem in a proof assistant.
conclusion: This work establishes a foundation for verified development of advanced nonlinear programming algorithms.

title: Center-Fed Pinching Antenna System For Uplink Environment Sensing
authors: Cong Yu, Xu Gan, Bo Ai, Fellow, Yuanwei Liu, Wei Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A center-fed pinching antenna system (C-PASS)-enabled uplink environment sensing framework is proposed. Through the center-fed framework, doubled degrees of freedom is achieved compared to conventional end-fed PASS. Based on this, we consider an uplink sensing scenario, in which a linear inverse model is developed to reconstruct the environment through signals scattered by the environment object. In the proposed framework, the distance between the feed points for stable separation of the received signals is characterized in closed form. Furthermore, Ziv-Zakai bound (ZZB) expressions for the mean-squared reconstruction error are derived for C-PASS and end-fed PASS. Based on these theoretical results, it can be proved that C-PASS achieves a strictly lower reconstruction error bound than conventional PASS for uplink environment sensing. Finally, numerical results validate the accuracy of the derived ZZB expressions and 1) demonstrate that C-PASS provides more stable separation of the received signals, and 2) confirm the consistent performance advantages of C-PASS.
tldr: A center-fed pinching antenna system for uplink environment sensing is proposed, achieving lower reconstruction error bounds than conventional end-fed systems.
motivation: To improve environment sensing in wireless communication by increasing degrees of freedom and reducing reconstruction error.
method: A linear inverse model is developed, and Ziv-Zakai bounds are derived for both center-fed and end-fed pinching antenna systems.
result: Center-fed PASS achieves strictly lower reconstruction error bounds and more stable signal separation.
conclusion: The proposed C-PASS framework offers consistent performance advantages for uplink environment sensing.

title: Exact Dimensionality Of Projected Measures For Expanding Rational Semigroups
authors: Yuto Nakajima
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25474v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the dimension theory of expanding rational semigroups. An expanding rational semigroup is naturally described by a skew product on the product of the symbolic space and the Riemann sphere. For an invariant Borel probability measure of this skew product, we consider its disintegration over a symbolic factor and study the push-forwards of the conditional measures under the second coordinate projection. We prove a Ledrappier--Young type formula for the projected conditional measures. In particular, if the original invariant measure is ergodic, then these projected conditional measures are exact dimensional for almost every fiber. Applying this result to the trivial factor yields exact dimensionality of the projected invariant measure. This result can be viewed as a backward analogue of the result of [D.-J. Feng and H. Hu. (2009), no. 11, 1435--1500].
tldr: This paper proves exact dimensionality of projected measures for expanding rational semigroups using a Ledrappier-Young type formula.
motivation: To understand the dimension theory of expanding rational semigroups, which are dynamical systems on the Riemann sphere.
method: The paper studies invariant measures of a skew product and analyzes the push-forwards of conditional measures under projection, proving a Ledrappier-Young type formula.
result: The projected conditional measures are exact dimensional for almost every fiber, and the projected invariant measure is exact dimensional.
conclusion: The result provides a backward analogue of a known result by Feng and Hu, contributing to the dimension theory of rational semigroups.

title: Performance Analysis For Heterogeneous Air-Ground Isac In Coordinated Multipoint Networks
authors: Yihang Jiang, Xiaoyang Li, Guangxu Zhu, Changsheng You, Xiaowen Cao, Dingzhu Wen, Bingpeng Zhou, Xinyi Wang, Rui Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The emergence of the (LAE) calls for highly integrated and reliable wireless systems that can simultaneously support (C\&S) functions. Although (ISAC) has been widely studied, most existing works focused on link-level or single-cell architectures in terrestrial environments, leaving the potential of network-level cooperative air-ground ISAC largely unexplored. To bridge this gap, a heterogeneous air-ground ISAC network architecture based on (CoMP) is proposed, which incorporates a cooperative hybrid mono/bi-static sensing scheme to enhance spatial diversity and sensing capability. In the proposed architecture, a two-tier (BS) deployment is adopted: master BSs are arranged in a hexagonal lattice, while slave BSs follow a Poisson point process distribution. This structure concurrently supports communication for terrestrial users and sensing for aerial targets. A holistic performance analysis framework for both C\&S is further developed, accounting for key channel and network parameters. Simulation results reveal inherent trade-offs between C\&S performance, especially under multi-BS cooperation and varying network density. These findings provide practical guidance for the deployment of scalable and efficient ISAC networks in LAE scenarios.
tldr: This paper proposes a heterogeneous air-ground ISAC network architecture using coordinated multipoint (CoMP) to jointly support communication and sensing, focusing on performance trade-offs in large-scale deployments.
motivation: Existing ISAC studies focus on link-level or single-cell terrestrial architectures, leaving network-level cooperative air-ground ISAC unexplored. The paper aims to bridge this gap for low-altitude economy (LAE) scenarios.
method: A two-tier base station deployment (master BSs in hexagonal lattice, slave BSs via Poisson point process) is combined with a cooperative hybrid mono/bi-static sensing scheme. A performance analysis framework accounting for channel and network parameters is developed and simulated.
result: Simulations reveal inherent trade-offs between communication and sensing performance under multi-BS cooperation and varying network density.
conclusion: The findings provide practical guidance for deploying scalable and efficient ISAC networks in LAE scenarios.

title: How A Computer Might Think
authors: Sankha S. Basu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24927v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inspired by Nuel Belnap's "How a computer should think," which gave rise to the four-valued logic FDE, we contemplate, in this article, how a computer might think if we add a fifth value for unknowable or cannot be known. We devise two new five-valued logics, UKN1 and UKN2, called the logics of the unknowable. These are different from the five-valued logic FDEe of the FDE-family. The main difference is in the number of designated truth values. While FDEe takes two designated values, UKN1 and UKN2 have three. The four-valued reducts of these logics are also different from FDE. This is due to the fact that instead of taking one of the non-designated values as neither true nor false, as in FDE, we have interpreted this as not known yet. This value although denoted by the same letter [MATH], behaves differently from its namesake in FDE.
tldr: The paper proposes two five-valued logics (UKN1 and UKN2) for modeling unknowable propositions, extending Belnap's four-valued logic FDE.
motivation: To explore how a computer might reason about propositions that are unknowable or cannot be known, building on Belnap's work on how a computer should think.
method: The author defines two five-valued logics with three designated truth values, differing from existing five-valued logics like FDEe, and analyzes their four-valued reducts.
result: Two new five-valued logics are presented, with distinct designated values and behavior of the 'neither true nor false' value reinterpreted as 'not known yet'.
conclusion: The logics offer a novel approach to handling unknowable information, but the work is purely logical and philosophical, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Intractability Of Hilbert's Nullstellensatz Implies Algebraic Hardness Of Permanent
authors: Peter B\"urgisser
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the logical relation of the P-NP separation conjecture in the Blum-Shub-Smale-model over the complex numbers with the P-NP separation conjecture in Valiant's algebraic model. This amounts to comparing Hilbert's Nullstellensatz Problem, that is, deciding feasibility of a given system of polynomial equations over the complex numbers, with the problem of evaluating the permanent of a given complex matrix. We compare the respective uniform models of computations and prove that [MATH] in the Blum-Shub-Smale-model over [MATH] implies the separation [MATH] of the uniform versions of Valiant's constant-free complexity classes over [MATH]. For the nonuniform models we show the analogous implication: the separation [MATH] of the nonuniform, constant-free Blum-Shub-Smale classes over [MATH] implies the separation [MATH] of Valiant's constant-free complexity classes over [MATH]. In the reverse direction, we conjecture that [MATH] implies that [MATH].
tldr: This paper explores the relationship between the P vs. NP problem in the Blum-Shub-Smale model over complex numbers and Valiant's algebraic complexity classes, focusing on the permanent and Hilbert's Nullstellensatz.
motivation: To understand the logical connections between different models of algebraic computation and complexity separations.
method: The paper compares uniform and nonuniform complexity classes in the Blum-Shub-Smale model and Valiant's model, proving implications between separations.
result: It shows that P ≠ NP in the Blum-Shub-Smale model implies VP ≠ VNP in Valiant's constant-free model, and similarly for nonuniform classes.
conclusion: The results establish a bridge between two major complexity conjectures, suggesting that proving algebraic hardness of the permanent is at least as hard as separating P and NP over the complex numbers.

title: Homomorphic Encryptions For Privacy Preserving Vision
authors: Preey Shah, Rohan Virani, Sanjari Srivastava
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Legal requirements might prevent organizations from sharing sensitive data like medical or financial details of consumers which prevents them from leveraging cloud based ML-as-a-service solutions provided by third party providers, which are quickly gaining popularity these days. In this project, we aim to perform inference tasks in Computer Vision in a privacy-preserving manner, i.e, by only looking at encrypted data. Recent advances in fully homomorphic encryption make this possible. A fully homomorphic encryption allows an arbitrary sequence of additive and multiplicative operations to be performed on encrypted data directly. Applying homomorphic encryptions to CNNs requires modifying the conventional CNN layers, so that they adhere to the encryption scheme. Our aim was to explore the best methods to create CNNs which can classify encrypted images directly. We used Microsoft SEAL for performing homomorphic encryption. The performance of these "encryption based CNNs" should be comparable with baseline accuracies of the same CNNs trained on unencrypted data, and the aim was to achieve as low of a hit on inference-time performance as possible. We successfully obtained minimal drop in classification accuracy for various datasets. We used MNIST as our baseline, which is popularly used in related research work and then explored more complex datasets like Kuzushiji MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 as a part of our contribution. Additionally, we also added support for more complex operations on top of TenSEAL, like processing colored images (multi-channel input), applying multiple convolutional layers and performing average pooling.
tldr: This paper applies fully homomorphic encryption to convolutional neural networks for privacy-preserving image classification.
motivation: Legal restrictions prevent sharing sensitive data, hindering use of cloud ML services; homomorphic encryption allows inference on encrypted data.
method: Modified CNN layers to be compatible with the Microsoft SEAL homomorphic encryption scheme, supporting multi-channel inputs, multiple convolutions, and average pooling.
result: Achieved minimal drop in classification accuracy on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, Kuzushiji-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 with acceptable inference time overhead.
conclusion: Homomorphic encryption can enable privacy-preserving computer vision with practical accuracy and performance trade-offs.

title: Sponsored Group Signature And Its Application To Privacy-preserving Guest Access In Smart Environments
authors: Sepideh Avizheh, Reihaneh Safavi-Naini, Shiwei Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Group signatures are privacy preserving signature schemes in which a group member can anonymously sign messages on behalf of the group, while providing accountability, by allowing the signature of a misbehaving group member be ``opened'' and the identity of the signer be revealed. In group signature members are admitted to the group by a (trusted) group manager. We motivate the need for a flexible mechanism in applications, such as privacy preserving access in smart environments, and propose a two-level member-join group signature that we call SPonsored Group Signature (SPGS) where group members of level 1 can ``sponsor'' new members, in level 2, to join the group. This relaxation of user join comes with additional accountability mechanisms: we require that the signature of a sponsored member can be opened to the identity of the sponsor (that is sponsor is responsible for the sponsored member), and while all signatures are anonymous, for the sponsored members, the signatures are linkable. This allows a sponsor to efficiently identify an undesirable sponsored member. We formalize SPGS scheme, define its security using a game-based approach, and give a generic construction of SPGS that uses a (dynamic) group signature scheme, a commitment scheme, and a knowledge-sound non-interactive zero knowledge proof of knowledge, and prove its security. We also give an instantiation of our construction. To show applicability of SPGS in practice, we consider the problem of providing guest access in a smart building, and introduce Anonymous Guest Access Token (AGAT) that allows a temporary guest to anonymously access (a subset of) the building resources. We show how SPGS can be used (together with an IND-CPA secure public key encryption scheme) to give a direct construction for AGAT, and show the efficiency of our guest access protocol when it is instantiated with existing schemes.
tldr: This paper proposes a sponsored group signature scheme for privacy-preserving guest access in smart environments.
motivation: Existing group signatures lack flexibility for scenarios where existing members can sponsor new members, such as guest access in smart buildings.
method: The authors formalize SPGS with two-level membership, define security games, and give a generic construction using a dynamic group signature, commitment scheme, and NIZK proof.
result: They provide a security proof and an instantiation, and show how SPGS can be used to construct an Anonymous Guest Access Token (AGAT) protocol.
conclusion: SPGS enables flexible and accountable member sponsorship while preserving privacy, with practical efficiency for smart environment access control.

title: Information Flow Security On Persistent Memory
authors: Graeme Smith
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Persistent memory is a recently proposed memory paradigm that delivers many system-wide benefits, including improved runtime efficiency and the ability of programs to recover from power outages and system crashes. While recent research has investigated techniques for proving functional correctness of programs running on related architectures, this is not the case for the orthogonal concept of information flow security. In this paper, we provide an information flow logic for an unstructured language (i.e., with gotos rather than loops) modelling a simple assembly language. We apply this logic to x86 assembly using a notion of reordering interference freedom (rif) to reason about potential out-of-order propagation of instructions to memory. We then show how this same notion of rif can be used to similarly reason about information flow on persistent memory.
tldr: This paper presents an information flow logic for persistent memory architectures, focusing on security in assembly-level programs.
motivation: Persistent memory offers system benefits but introduces new security challenges for information flow; existing work on functional correctness does not address security.
method: The authors develop an information flow logic for an unstructured language with gotos, model x86 assembly, and use a notion of reordering interference freedom to reason about out-of-order propagation to memory.
result: The logic is applied to x86 assembly and shown to also reason about information flow on persistent memory.
conclusion: The proposed logic provides a foundation for verifying information flow security in persistent memory systems.

title: CrypFormBench: Benchmarking Formal Analysis Capability Of Large Language Models For Cryptographic Schemes
authors: Zhaoxuan Li, Qionglu Zhang, Hengyuan Liu, Xiaoyan Gu, Xianhui Lu, Hongbo Liu, Bingzheng Wang, Haihui Fan, Ziming Zhao, Rui Zhang, Li Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25561v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Manual formal analysis of cryptographic schemes is labor-intensive and requires substantial expertise. While model-checking tools (e.g., Scyther and Tamarin) and computational-security tools (e.g., CryptoVerif and EasyCrypt) improve the automation of security proofs, they still rely on experts to abstract schemes and write tool-specific formal descriptions. Large language models (LLMs) are a promising alternative, but their effectiveness in this domain remains unexplored due to the absence of standardized evaluation methodologies. To fill this gap, we introduce CrypFormBench (C.F.B for short), a comprehensive benchmark jointly covering symbolic and computational security to evaluate five core LLM capabilities: interpretation, generation, completion, transformation, and correction. It comprises 700 instances spanning 677 schemes, 7 mainstream formal verifier languages, and 160 security properties. The evaluation of 9 state-of-the-art LLMs reveals that most of them perform well on interpretation and completion, given their code-awareness advantages, but struggle with generation, transformation, and correction. Overall, their performance remains limited, with Claude-3.5 achieving the highest score at 48.7 out of 100. We further provide practical guidance, e.g., few-shot prompting, Pass@K sampling, and lightweight fine-tuning, to mitigate the executability bottleneck and improve tool-usable outputs. Taken together, our benchmark and analyses offer a grounded view of current progress and concrete directions toward reliable LLM-assisted formal cryptographic analysis.
tldr: This paper introduces a benchmark for evaluating large language models on formal analysis of cryptographic schemes, focusing on symbolic and computational security proofs.
motivation: Manual formal analysis of cryptographic schemes is labor-intensive and requires expertise; LLMs offer a potential alternative but lack standardized evaluation.
method: The authors create CrypFormBench, a benchmark with 700 instances covering 677 schemes, 7 formal verifier languages, and 160 security properties, testing five LLM capabilities: interpretation, generation, completion, transformation, and correction.
result: Evaluation of 9 state-of-the-art LLMs shows they perform well on interpretation and completion but struggle with generation, transformation, and correction; Claude-3.5 achieves the highest score of 48.7/100.
conclusion: LLMs currently have limited effectiveness for formal cryptographic analysis, but few-shot prompting, Pass@K sampling, and fine-tuning can mitigate some bottlenecks.

title: Privacy Vulnerabilities Of Attention Layers In Tabular Foundation Models And Protection Of High-Risk Queries
authors: Maxime Cordy T\^ania Carvalho
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tabular foundation models are commonly assumed to present limited privacy concerns as they are often pre-trained on large collections of synthetic data. However, these models leverage in-context learning, where sensitive records may be provided directly at inference time as labelled context examples. In this paper, we demonstrate that predictions generated via the attention mechanism leak sufficient information to enable effective Membership Inference Attacks (MIAs). To highlight this vulnerability, we propose AMIA (Attention-based Membership Inference Attack), a shadow-model-free attack that exploits the concentration of transformer attention patterns. Our results show that attention mechanisms reveal strong membership signals, which exceed classical confidence-based attacks, achieving an average gain of 7.7\%, specially in low false-positive regimes. To mitigate this risk, we introduce an inference-time defence inspired by [MATH]-anonymity principles. This approach reduces the uniqueness of context-key representations without introducing random noise or retraining the model. By targeting only high-risk queries identified through AMIA scores, the defence substantially reduces membership leakage of this attack by an average of 50\% and 25\% against confidence-based attacks, while preserving predictive utility with only 3.9\% performance degradation. Beyond showing that context examples are vulnerable, we further demonstrate that fine-tuning introduces an additional source of privacy risk. In particular, samples whose prediction confidence increases after fine-tuning become more susceptible to MIAs, indicating that fine-tuning can amplify memorisation and expose sensitive training information through confidence shifts.
tldr: This paper studies privacy vulnerabilities in attention layers of tabular foundation models, proposing a membership inference attack and a defense mechanism.
motivation: Tabular foundation models are assumed to have limited privacy concerns, but in-context learning with sensitive records may leak information via attention mechanisms.
method: The authors propose AMIA, a shadow-model-free membership inference attack exploiting attention pattern concentration, and a defense based on k-anonymity principles applied to context-key representations.
result: AMIA achieves an average gain of 7.7% over confidence-based attacks, and the defense reduces membership leakage by 50% against AMIA and 25% against confidence-based attacks with only 3.9% performance degradation.
conclusion: Attention mechanisms in tabular foundation models are vulnerable to membership inference, and the proposed defense effectively mitigates this risk without retraining.

title: Can Trustless Agents Be Trusted? An Empirical Study Of The Erc-8004 Decentralized Ai Agent Ecosystem
authors: Xihan Xiong, Zelin Li, Wei Wei, Qin Wang, William Knottenbelt, Zhipeng Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26028v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As autonomous AI agents increasingly transact across organizational boundaries, a fundamental trust challenge emerges: how can an agent assess whether an unknown counterpart is trustworthy? The ERC-8004 protocol addresses this challenge with the first permissionless trust layer for AI agent economies, built around three on-chain registries for Identity, Reputation, and Validation. Despite its rapid adoption, the protocol has not been studied empirically, leaving it unclear whether the information it records provides a trustworthy basis for decision-making. To address this gap, we present the first empirical study of ERC-8004 across three chains: Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain (BSC), and Base, covering the period from protocol deployment through May 13, 2026. We crawl on-chain Identity and Reputation events, off-chain files, and x402 payment transactions. On the identity side, we find that most registrations are placeholders rather than active agents, with only a small fraction (3%, 4%, and 15% across Ethereum, BSC, and Base) exposing a valid ERC-8004 registration file with at least one live service endpoint. On the reputation side, we show that the Registry, as currently deployed, cannot function as a trust signal: values are not commensurable, feedback records are rarely grounded in verifiable interactions, and reputation can be manipulated at minimal cost. Consistent with these design weaknesses, we find that a substantial fraction of reviewers (73.6%, 59.2%, and 90.6% across Ethereum, BSC, and Base) exhibit coordinated Sybil behavior. After removing Sybil-flagged feedback, 15.5%, 72.3%, and 89.4% of rated agents, respectively, are left with no valid feedback. We then turn these findings into concrete recommendations for future revisions of ERC-8004. Our study yields actionable protocol-design implications and establishes an empirical baseline for research on AI agent markets.
tldr: An empirical study of the ERC-8004 decentralized AI agent trust protocol on Ethereum, BSC, and Base, finding that most registrations are placeholders and reputation signals are unreliable due to Sybil attacks.
motivation: To assess whether the ERC-8004 protocol provides trustworthy information for AI agents to evaluate unknown counterparts, given its rapid adoption but lack of empirical scrutiny.
method: Crawled on-chain Identity and Reputation events, off-chain files, and x402 payment transactions across three blockchains from deployment to May 2026, analyzing registration validity, reputation commensurability, and Sybil behavior.
result: Only 3-15% of registrations have valid endpoints; reputation values are not commensurable, feedback is rarely verifiable, and 59-91% of reviewers exhibit coordinated Sybil behavior, leaving most agents without valid feedback after filtering.
conclusion: The current ERC-8004 implementation cannot serve as a reliable trust layer; concrete recommendations for protocol revisions are provided.

title: Nonlinear Lissajous Orbits And Particular Superintegrability
authors: R. Azuaje A. M. Escobar-Ruiz
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the geometry of classical trajectories generated by separable two-dimensional polynomial potentials of the form [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH]. Special emphasis is placed on the emergence of nonlinear Lissajous figures and on the distinction between global and particular superintegrability in the Liouville sense. In the harmonic case ([MATH]) closed periodic orbits are a consequence of an additional integral of motion whenever the frequency ratio is rational, rendering the system maximally superintegrable. In contrast, for anharmonic oscillators, already in the quartic case ([MATH]), the oscillation frequencies depend on the partial energies, so periodic Lissajous-type trajectories occur only under nonlinear resonance conditions fixed by the initial data. Accordingly, the extra conserved quantities that characterize these closed orbits are not global invariants but (trajectory-dependent) integrals that emerge only on the resonant trajectories. For higher-degree potentials [MATH], the resonant trajectories are naturally described by hyperelliptic phase constraints rather than by a universal polynomial orbit equation.
tldr: The paper studies classical trajectories in separable polynomial potentials, focusing on nonlinear Lissajous figures and superintegrability.
motivation: To understand the geometry of classical orbits and distinguish between global and particular superintegrability in anharmonic systems.
method: Analytical and geometric analysis of two-dimensional polynomial potentials, examining periodic orbits and conserved quantities.
result: Nonlinear Lissajous orbits occur only under resonance conditions; extra integrals are trajectory-dependent, not global.
conclusion: The work clarifies the nature of superintegrability in anharmonic oscillators, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Zipf's Law Before The Monetary Economy And Written Administration: Volume Distribution Of Kofun, Ancient Japanese Burial Mounds
authors: Hayafumi Watanabe
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study analyzes the volume distribution of kofun, large mounded tombs constructed in the Japanese archipelago from the mid- to late third into the early seventh century. This period provides a rare empirical case for examining the distribution of politico-economic resources and mobilizing capacity in a society where systematic written records of administrative and economic transactions had not yet become established. Using a large-scale database containing mound length, height, and shape, we estimate kofun volumes and examine their distributions at the archipelago-wide scale and by region, period, and mound type. We find that the volume distribution of keyhole-shaped kofun exhibits a Zipf-like tail, with a cumulative power-law exponent close to unity, indicating strong concentration of volume among a small number of top-ranked tombs. At the same time, the central part of the distribution is close to log-normal. Many regional and temporal differences can be described primarily as scale differences: after normalization by the median, the distributions for many regions and periods approximately collapse onto a common curve. However, some exceptional regions and periods, most notably the politically central Kinki region, show heavier tails and stronger concentration among the largest kofun. To interpret these empirical regularities, we introduce a simple Kesten-type stochastic growth model with stopping and reorganization. The model provides a unified interpretation in which the log-normal-like body, the Zipf-like tail, and aspects of regional and temporal variation in the distributions arise from a common growth process. These results suggest that collectively mobilized resources may already have exhibited a Zipf-like concentration structure statistically comparable to that observed in modern firm sales distributions.
tldr: This paper analyzes the volume distribution of ancient Japanese burial mounds (kofun) and finds a Zipf-like tail, suggesting concentration of resources similar to modern firm sales.
motivation: To understand the distribution of politico-economic resources in a pre-monetary, pre-literate society using archaeological data.
method: Estimates kofun volumes from a large database of mound dimensions, fits power-law and log-normal distributions, and introduces a Kesten-type stochastic growth model.
result: Keyhole-shaped kofun volumes exhibit a Zipf-like tail (exponent ~1) and a log-normal body; regional variations collapse after normalization, except for the politically central Kinki region.
conclusion: Collectively mobilized resources in ancient Japan followed a concentration pattern similar to modern economies, suggesting universal statistical regularities.

title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks For The Time-Domain Maxwell Equations With Split-Field Perfectly Matched Layers
authors: Xiaodong Liu, Lingquan Li, Gregory Moss, Scott Langdon
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics informed neural networks (PINNs) incorporate Maxwell's equations, initial conditions, boundary conditions, and measurement data directly into the learning process, transforming the solution of partial differential equations into a constrained optimization problem. As such, PINNs are attracting increased attention in computational electromagnetics as an alternative to traditional time-domain solvers. This paper presents a PINN formulation for the time-domain Maxwell's equations incorporating split-field perfectly matched layers (PMLs). A key advantage of the split-field PML formulation is that the same governing equations can be applied in both the physical and PML regions, simplifying the PINN formulation and loss construction. The proposed approach is validated using one-dimensional and two-dimensional Gaussian pulse problems with PML. The PINN solutions show good agreement with analytical and finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) reference solutions, demonstrating the feasibility of combining PINNs with split-field PMLs for open-domain time-domain electromagnetic simulations.
tldr: This paper applies physics-informed neural networks to solve time-domain Maxwell's equations with split-field perfectly matched layers for open-domain electromagnetic simulations.
motivation: Traditional time-domain solvers for Maxwell's equations can be computationally expensive; PINNs offer a mesh-free alternative that incorporates physical laws directly into the learning process.
method: The authors formulate a PINN that incorporates Maxwell's equations, initial/boundary conditions, and split-field PML equations into a loss function, and train the network to satisfy these constraints.
result: The PINN solutions show good agreement with analytical and FDTD reference solutions for 1D and 2D Gaussian pulse problems with PML.
conclusion: Combining PINNs with split-field PMLs is feasible for open-domain time-domain electromagnetic simulations, providing an alternative to traditional numerical methods.

title: Pseudo-spectral Frequency-domain Method With Background Field Decomposition And Green's Function Preconditioner For Electromagnetic Scattering Problem In Euv Lithography
authors: Seungjin Lee, Werner Gillijns, Doyun Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide an accelerated computational framework to solve electromagnetic scattering problems in planarly layered media arising from extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography. To achieve this, we reformulate the EUV scattering problem into a scattering problem on a homogeneous background, in which the electromagnetic contribution of the layered media is captured by a recursively updated reflection of the layered stack. The system is numerically solved by employing the pseudo-spectral frequency-domain method paired with an iterative solver, whose iterative convergence is expedited by a free-space Green's function preconditioner. The proposed framework is evaluated on EUV mask geometries and multilayer mirror stacks, demonstrating a significant speedup over the conventional pseudo-spectral frequency-domain method.
tldr: This paper presents a computational method for electromagnetic scattering in EUV lithography, unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: EUV lithography requires efficient simulation of electromagnetic scattering in layered media to improve mask design and imaging.
method: The authors reformulate the scattering problem using background field decomposition and a free-space Green's function preconditioner within a pseudo-spectral frequency-domain method.
result: The proposed framework achieves significant speedup over conventional methods for EUV mask and multilayer mirror geometries.
conclusion: The method provides an accelerated computational tool for EUV lithography scattering problems.

title: On Common Values Of $F_n$ And Nathanson's Totient Function $\Phi(m)$
authors: Sagar Mandal
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a recent paper, Chatterjee, the author and Mohan posed the problem of determining all solutions of the Diophantine equation [MATH], where [MATH] is the [MATH]-th Fibonacci number and [MATH] counts the number of nonempty sets [MATH] for which [MATH] is relatively prime to [MATH]. In this paper, we prove that the Diophantine equation has the only solutions [MATH]. The main tools used in this paper are lower bounds for linear forms in logarithms due to Matveev and Dujella-Peth{} version of the Baker-Davenport reduction method in diophantine approximation.
tldr: This paper solves a Diophantine equation involving Fibonacci numbers and Nathanson's totient function using linear forms in logarithms.
motivation: To find all common values between Fibonacci numbers and a specific totient function, extending previous work.
method: Uses lower bounds for linear forms in logarithms (Matveev) and the Baker-Davenport reduction method.
conclusion: The Diophantine equation has only finitely many solutions, all found explicitly.

title: Spectral Riccati--Gamma Concavity, Symmetric Zero Cancellation, And Conditional Criteria For The Riemann Hypothesis
authors: Dragos-Patru Covei
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine a Riccati--Gamma approach to the logarithmic derivative of the completed Riemann zeta function. The first part proves, in full local detail, that a naive two-sided vertical concavity criterion for [MATH] cannot be a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, because every zero produces opposite vertical curvatures on the two horizontal sides of the pole of the logarithmic derivative. The second part replaces this obstruction by a rigorously formulated finite spectral averaging framework. We prove cancellation at the critical line, positivity of the off-critical paired contribution on the left of the critical line under a concrete low-frequency kernel condition, a conditional zero-density consequence, and a precise conditional theorem showing which additional localisation hypotheses would imply the Riemann Hypothesis. The results are therefore not presented as an unconditional proof of RH; rather, they isolate verifiable analytic assumptions under which the Riemann problem receives an affirmative answer. Reproducible Python routines and numerical figures accompany the analytic discussion.
tldr: This paper investigates analytic properties of the Riemann zeta function using a Riccati-Gamma approach, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The Riemann Hypothesis is a central problem in number theory; the authors aim to clarify obstacles and provide conditional criteria for its proof.
method: The authors analyze the logarithmic derivative of the completed zeta function via Riccati-Gamma equations, develop a spectral averaging framework, and provide numerical simulations.
result: They prove that a naive concavity criterion cannot prove the Riemann Hypothesis, and they derive conditional results that would imply the hypothesis under additional localization assumptions.
conclusion: The paper does not provide an unconditional proof but isolates verifiable analytic assumptions that could lead to a proof.

title: Wideband Near-Field Channel Estimation Under Hybrid Compression: Cross-Subcarrier Kl Covariance Fitting With Ofdm Fresnel Model
authors: R{\i}fat Volkan \c{s}enyuva
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider wideband channel estimation for extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) arrays under hybrid analog-digital compression, in which a uniform linear array (ULA) is observed through far fewer radio-frequency (RF) chains than antennas. At a carrier frequency of 28 GHz with bandwidths reaching several hundred MHz, the standard narrowband polar-domain channel model fails: the near-field Fresnel curvature becomes subcarrier-dependent, and the compressed observation destroys the per-subcarrier spatial covariance structure that narrowband methods exploit. We propose the Wideband Cross-subcarrier Kullback--Leibler (WB-CL-KL) estimator, which jointly estimates angle and range directly from the compressed sample covariance, without full-array reconstruction, by fitting a structured Fresnel covariance model across orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) subcarriers via a cross-subcarrier Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence criterion. We also derive the wideband compressed-domain Cram\'er--Rao bound (CRB) -- the performance lower bound for this hybrid architecture -- from the Slepian--Bangs formula, and decompose its gain over the narrowband bound into a data-diversity component of +27.093 dB and a geometric-diversity component of +0.701 dB, totalling +27.793 dB at B = 400 MHz (Propositions 1 and 2). In the single-path line-of-sight regime, WB-CL-KL attains a range root-mean-square error of 19.8 mm against a 19.9 mm bound at signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) = 10 dB, a ratio of 0.996. Under the 3GPP Urban Micro (UMi) path-loss and shadow-fading SNR distribution, it achieves a bound ratio of 0.959 at the median deployment SNR of 9.6 dB, indicating near-CRB operation at the representative deployment point, where the compressed-domain bound is evaluated at the scene-median geometry.
tldr: This paper proposes a wideband near-field channel estimation method for XL-MIMO systems using hybrid analog-digital compression and OFDM, focusing on angle and range estimation via cross-subcarrier covariance fitting.
motivation: Standard narrowband channel models fail for wideband XL-MIMO due to subcarrier-dependent Fresnel curvature and compressed observations that destroy per-subcarrier covariance structure.
method: The WB-CL-KL estimator jointly estimates angle and range from compressed sample covariance by fitting a structured Fresnel covariance model across OFDM subcarriers using a cross-subcarrier KL divergence criterion.
result: The estimator achieves near-CRB performance, with range RMSE of 19.8 mm against a 19.9 mm bound at SNR=10 dB, and a bound ratio of 0.959 at median deployment SNR.
conclusion: The proposed method enables accurate near-field channel estimation under hybrid compression, with performance close to the theoretical lower bound.

title: Minimization Of A One Class Of Maximum Functions With Applications To Some Eigenvalue Problems
authors: \.ipek Cafer Ismayilov, Taner B\"uy\"ukk\"oro\u{g}lu, Vakif Dzhafarov
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25106v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we consider the problem of minimization of a convex function that can be expressed as a maximum of affine linear functions. A convergence theorem is established and the minimizing sequence is constructed. The computational time is linear with respect to the step number. The obtained results are applied to eigenvalue problems such as eigenvalue minimization, symmetric stabilization, and the Riccati matrix inequalities. A number of examples are provided.
tldr: This paper presents a convex optimization method for minimizing a maximum of affine functions and applies it to eigenvalue problems.
motivation: To develop an efficient algorithm for minimizing convex functions expressed as a maximum of affine linear functions, with applications to eigenvalue problems.
method: The authors construct a minimizing sequence and prove a convergence theorem; the computational time is linear in the step number.
result: The method is applied to eigenvalue minimization, symmetric stabilization, and Riccati matrix inequalities, with examples provided.
conclusion: The proposed algorithm is effective for the considered class of problems and has linear computational complexity.

title: No 3d Matrices: A Unified Tensor-Product View Of Matrix-Free Cartesian Pde Solvers
authors: Kathleen A. Yearick Yong Yi Bay
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25148v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every Cartesian three-dimensional PDE solver hides a structural secret that production CFD codes have used for half a century and that graduate-level textbooks rarely state plainly. The derivative matrices, the compact Pad\'e line solves, the Galerkin mass inversions, the alternating-direction-implicit substeps, and even the fast Poisson and Helmholtz diagonalization transforms all factor along the coordinate axes and collapse into repeated one-dimensional banded kernels executed along the grid lines. The three-dimensional operator exists only on paper; it is never assembled, factored, or stored. This paper is the manual for that collapse. We derive the Kronecker-product algebra that makes it exact, carry it cleanly through central differences, compact schemes, tensor-product Galerkin, B-spline and isogeometric methods, collocation, ADI time stepping, and direct Poisson and Helmholtz solves, and bring into the open the three production tricks that turn the reduction into hardware-conscious floating-point throughput on real machines: the multi-right-hand-side reshape that exposes a sweep as one batched line kernel (a dense BLAS-3 GEMM when the line factor is dense or element-local, a banded or stencil kernel when it is not), the sum factorization that rescues high-order Galerkin from the [MATH] quadrature trap, and the pencil decomposition that keeps every direction contiguous across an MPI cluster. For fixed stencil width or fixed polynomial degree, the compute cost stays [MATH] in the total number of unknowns [MATH]; the operator storage drops to [MATH] up to bandwidth constants; direct separable Poisson and Helmholtz solvers add the expected transform cost; the line kernels are embarrassingly parallel. These facts are familiar to practitioners but rarely assembled in one place; this paper collects them and shows how to use them.
tldr: This paper presents a unified Kronecker-product framework for matrix-free Cartesian PDE solvers, showing that 3D operators can be decomposed into 1D line kernels.
motivation: To expose the structural secret behind efficient Cartesian PDE solvers and provide a comprehensive manual for implementing matrix-free methods.
method: Derives Kronecker-product algebra for central differences, compact schemes, tensor-product Galerkin, B-splines, collocation, ADI, and direct Poisson/Helmholtz solves, and describes production tricks like multi-RHS reshape, sum factorization, and pencil decomposition.
result: The compute cost is O(N) for fixed stencil width or polynomial degree, operator storage is O(N^{2/3}), and line kernels are embarrassingly parallel.
conclusion: The paper collects and explains well-known but scattered techniques for matrix-free Cartesian PDE solvers, serving as a practical guide for high-performance computing.

title: On The Linearization Of Alternative Means
authors: Raluca Dumitru, Jose Franco, Allan Merino
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Alternative means have recently attracted considerable attention in matrix analysis and operator theory. In this paper, we investigate the linearization problem for alternative means, namely the question of determining when a mean can be expressed as an affine combination of the matrices under consideration. We first prove a conjecture of Choi, Kim, and Lim for the Wasserstein mean. More precisely, we show that the Wasserstein mean [MATH] is linearizable if and only if [MATH] and [MATH]. We further establish a general rigidity theorem for a large class of alternative means. Specifically, we prove that an analogous characterization holds whenever the representing function [MATH] is of the form [MATH], where [MATH] is a non-affine operator monotone function. As consequences, we obtain linearization criteria for several families of alternative means, including logarithmic, harmonic, and power-type means.
tldr: The paper studies linearization of alternative means in matrix analysis, proving a conjecture about the Wasserstein mean and establishing a rigidity theorem for operator monotone functions.
motivation: To determine when an alternative mean can be expressed as an affine combination of matrices, which is a fundamental question in matrix analysis and operator theory.
method: The authors use techniques from matrix analysis and operator monotone functions, proving a conjecture by Choi, Kim, and Lim for the Wasserstein mean and extending the result to a general class of means.
result: The Wasserstein mean is linearizable if and only if the matrices commute; a similar characterization holds for means defined by non-affine operator monotone functions.
conclusion: The work provides a complete linearization criterion for several families of alternative means, contributing to the theory of matrix means.

title: Zero-Hopf Bifurcation Of Qi Hyperchaotic Systems
authors: Pedro Iv\'an Su\'arez Navarro Sonia Isabel Renteria Alva
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we show a zero-Hopf bifurcations in a four-dimensional hyperchaotic Qi system. While the hyperchaotic dynamics of this model have been extensively investigated, the existence and bifurcation of zero-Hopf equilibria have not been previously analyzed. We first characterize the equilibrium points and determine the parameter conditions under which the origin becomes a zero-Hopf equilibrium. Using second-order averaging theory, we establish the existence of up to four small amplitude periodic solutions bifurcating from the origin under suitable parameter perturbations. We also provide analytical expressions for the initial conditions of these solutions.
tldr: This paper studies zero-Hopf bifurcations in a four-dimensional hyperchaotic Qi system using second-order averaging theory.
motivation: The hyperchaotic Qi system has been studied extensively, but zero-Hopf bifurcations have not been analyzed before.
method: The authors characterize equilibrium points, determine conditions for zero-Hopf equilibrium, and apply second-order averaging theory to prove existence of periodic solutions.
result: Up to four small amplitude periodic solutions bifurcating from the origin are shown to exist under suitable parameter perturbations, with analytical expressions for initial conditions.
conclusion: The work provides a complete analysis of zero-Hopf bifurcations in the Qi hyperchaotic system, extending its dynamical understanding.

title: Classifying Groups Of Certain Orders
authors: Shihan Kanungo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We will first discuss the question of which integers [MATH] have exactly one group of order [MATH], namely the cyclic group [MATH]. We will see that these are the integers that are relatively prime to the Euler totient function [MATH]. Then we discuss how many groups there are of order [MATH] for each prime [MATH]. We end with a couple of interesting results and conjectures pertaining to groups of squarefree order.
tldr: This paper classifies groups of certain orders, focusing on cyclic groups and groups of prime and squarefree order.
motivation: To understand which integers have exactly one group of a given order and to count groups of prime and squarefree orders.
method: The paper uses group theory and number theory, discussing Euler's totient function and known results about group classification.
result: It characterizes integers with exactly one group (cyclic) as those coprime to Euler's totient function, and discusses group counts for prime and squarefree orders.
conclusion: The paper presents classical results and conjectures in group theory, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Structured Spectral Step-Sizes And A Hanoi Ordering Principle For Gradient Methods
authors: Ran Gu Yijia Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25311v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gradient methods are widely used for large-scale optimization, yet their practical convergence performance depends critically on step-size selection. However, a unified structural understanding of reliable spectral step sizes and a theoretically grounded mechanism for ordering step sequences remain underdeveloped. This paper addresses both gaps. We first establish a unified structural framework encompassing four families of spectral step sizes: the general Huang class, its rank-one subclass, the narrow Huang class, and the Gu-Du class. We rigorously characterize their inclusion relations and equivalence conditions. We then identify and analyze the rebound phenomenon in gradient iterations, whereby steps targeting low-frequency eigenvalues inadvertently amplify high-frequency gradient components. From this analysis, we derive the Hanoi ordering principle, which mandates recursive suppression of high-frequency components prior to each low-frequency step. This principle is further generalized to memory--m settings via a practical phase-wise recomputation strategy. Building on these foundations, we propose an adaptive Hanoi-like gradient method incorporating weighted component energy to select candidates and a settlement-continuation rule to compute the phase length for step reuse. We prove its global R-linear convergence for strictly convex quadratic objectives. Numerical experiments on ill-conditioned test problems demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms representative spectral gradient methods and the limited-memory BFGS method.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified framework for spectral step-sizes in gradient methods and introduces a Hanoi ordering principle for step sequences to improve convergence.
motivation: Gradient methods lack a unified structural understanding of reliable spectral step sizes and a theoretically grounded mechanism for ordering step sequences.
method: The authors establish a unified framework for four families of spectral step sizes, analyze the rebound phenomenon, derive the Hanoi ordering principle, and propose an adaptive gradient method with weighted component energy selection.
result: The proposed method achieves global R-linear convergence for strictly convex quadratic objectives and outperforms representative spectral gradient methods and L-BFGS on ill-conditioned test problems.
conclusion: The Hanoi ordering principle and adaptive method provide a principled approach to step-size selection and ordering in gradient methods.

title: Deterministic Non-Smooth Safety Via Dual-Algebraic Control Barrier Functions
authors: Mohammadreza Kamaldar
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25333v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a dual-algebraic framework for control barrier functions (CBFs) that guarantees deterministic execution using exclusively elementary arithmetic. We develop this deterministic approach to solve a fundamental bottleneck in safety-critical control: pointwise minima naturally compose intersecting safe sets, but generate non-smooth boundaries where standard Lie derivatives fail. Existing mathematical workarounds inject approximation bias, probabilistic non-determinism, or combinatorial execution delays that strictly impede hard real-time hardware certification. By embedding the system state and vector field into the dual-number ring, our method extracts both the composite barrier value and its exact directional derivative in a single evaluation. The standard floating-point minimum deterministically isolates a single vertex of the Clarke generalized gradient for the quadratic-program solver. We prove this selected vertex constitutes a valid Clarke subgradient and the resulting simultaneous-enforcement safety filter guarantees forward invariance. The arithmetic overhead remains a fixed constant factor, strictly independent of state dimension or constraint count. We extend this framework to arbitrary [MATH]/[MATH] Boolean compositions and systems of higher relative degree, validating the computational scaling on three physical examples.
tldr: A deterministic control barrier function framework using dual numbers for non-smooth safety-critical control.
motivation: Standard CBFs fail at non-smooth boundaries of composed safe sets, requiring approximations or non-determinism that hinder real-time certification.
method: Embeds system state and vector field into dual numbers to compute barrier value and directional derivative in one evaluation, selecting a valid Clarke subgradient via floating-point minimum.
result: The method guarantees forward invariance with fixed constant overhead independent of state dimension or constraint count, validated on three physical examples.
conclusion: The dual-algebraic approach provides a deterministic, efficient solution for safety filters with non-smooth constraints.

title: A Fully-decoupled Arbitrarily High-order Time-stepping Scheme Based On Matrix Diagonalization For The Anisotropic Phase-field Dendritic Crystal Growth Model
authors: Shaoqin Zheng Weiwen Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a fully-decoupled arbitrarily high-order time-stepping scheme for the anisotropic phase-field dendritic crystal growth model. The scheme combines an auxiliary-variable formulation with algebraically stable Runge-Kutta methods and satisfies a discrete energy dissipation law. To address the computational bottleneck arising from the coupled linear system in existing high-order schemes, a matrix diagonalization technique is introduced to transform the coupled linear elliptic system into a set of independent constant-coefficient elliptic equations. The resulting equations can be solved separately and in parallel, thereby improving computational efficiency. Numerical experiments in both two and three dimensions are presented to verify the convergence, energy stability, and efficiency of the proposed scheme. Comparisons with the original coupled formulation demonstrate the effectiveness of the matrix diagonalization strategy, while additional tests illustrate the advantages of high-order temporal discretizations. Simulations under different anisotropy coefficients, latent heat parameters, rotation angles, and initial nucleus shapes are also presented to investigate their effects on dendritic morphology.
tldr: This paper presents a high-order numerical scheme for simulating anisotropic phase-field dendritic crystal growth, focusing on computational efficiency via matrix diagonalization.
motivation: Existing high-order schemes for phase-field models suffer from coupled linear systems that are computationally expensive; the authors aim to develop a fully-decoupled, efficient scheme.
method: The scheme combines an auxiliary-variable formulation with algebraically stable Runge-Kutta methods and introduces a matrix diagonalization technique to decouple the linear system into independent constant-coefficient elliptic equations.
result: Numerical experiments in 2D and 3D verify convergence, energy stability, and efficiency; the matrix diagonalization strategy significantly reduces computational cost compared to the coupled formulation.
conclusion: The proposed scheme enables arbitrarily high-order temporal accuracy while maintaining full decoupling and parallelizability, making it suitable for large-scale phase-field simulations.

title: Quantitative Wasserstein Propagation Of Chaos For Transport Ensemble Filters
authors: Frederic J. N. Jorgensen, Ricardo Baptista, Franca Hoffmann, Youssef Marzouk
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a general probabilistic framework for analyzing propagation of chaos in transport ensemble filters (TEFs), a broad class of interacting particle systems that are used to approximate the sequence of state distributions in hidden Markov models given a history of observations. This class of transport-based filtering algorithms includes the widely used ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF), based on affine updates at each filtering step, as well as the ensemble stochastic map filter (EnSMF), which employs nonlinear updates. For this class, we identify the limiting mean-field dynamics. We then establish non-asymptotic, high-probability, pathwise Wasserstein convergence of the interacting particle system to an i.i.d. ensemble drawn from this mean-field limit at the Monte Carlo rate. Convergence to the mean-field law itself follows with the usual dimension-dependent empirical Wasserstein rate. The proof combines a synchronous coupling construction with stability of moments and tails under conditioning, together with quantitative estimates for the propagation of the underlying dynamics through the interacting particle system. Applying our theory to both the EnKF and the EnSMF yields the first non-asymptotic, high-probability convergence guarantees for TEFs.
tldr: This paper develops a probabilistic framework for analyzing propagation of chaos in transport ensemble filters, with non-asymptotic convergence guarantees.
motivation: Transport ensemble filters are widely used in data assimilation, but their theoretical convergence properties were not well understood.
method: The authors identify mean-field dynamics and use synchronous coupling with stability of moments and tails under conditioning to prove Wasserstein convergence.
result: They establish non-asymptotic, high-probability, pathwise Wasserstein convergence at the Monte Carlo rate for the interacting particle system to the mean-field limit.
conclusion: The framework provides the first non-asymptotic convergence guarantees for ensemble Kalman filters and ensemble stochastic map filters.

title: Primal-Dual Halpern-PAGE Algorithm For Constrained Stochastic Weakly Convex Optimization
authors: Lixin Tang, Xingyu Wang, Liwei Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We tackle the challenging problem of stochastic weakly convex optimization subject to mixed (equality and inequality) expected-value constraints. While optimal [MATH] sample complexity algorithms exist for unconstrained weakly convex problems, dealing with complex functional constraints typically requires cumbersome multi-loop penalty or augmented Lagrangian methods, which suffer from high inner-loop complexity and sensitive parameter tuning. To bridge this fundamental gap, we propose the primal-dual Halpern-PAGE (PD-HP) algorithm. As a purely single-loop method, PD-HP completely bypasses the computational burden of nested iterations. At each step, it merely requires solving a simple strongly convex surrogate subproblem alongside a straightforward dual projection, making it exceptionally efficient and convenient to implement. Crucially, we prove that this computationally lightweight algorithm achieves the optimal [MATH] sample complexity for mixed-constrained stochastic weakly convex problems, successfully matching the theoretical lower bounds. Furthermore, when the primal domain is a compact polyhedral convex set, we establish the deterministic stability of the dual multipliers by exploiting the generalized Mangasarian-Fromovitz constraint qualification (MFCQ) alongside Hoffman's error bound. This ensures that our optimal complexity bound holds strictly under the standard, unbounded KKT residual metric without any theoretical gaps or artificial residual truncations.
tldr: This paper proposes a primal-dual algorithm for constrained stochastic weakly convex optimization, unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: Stochastic weakly convex optimization with mixed constraints is challenging; existing methods are multi-loop and parameter-sensitive.
method: The primal-dual Halpern-PAGE algorithm is a single-loop method solving a strongly convex surrogate subproblem and a dual projection per iteration.
result: The algorithm achieves optimal sample complexity for mixed-constrained stochastic weakly convex problems, matching theoretical lower bounds.
conclusion: PD-HP provides an efficient, single-loop solution with optimal complexity, avoiding nested iterations and sensitive tuning.

title: Learning Optimization Proxies For Sequential Contextual Stochastic Programs: An Order Fulfillment Application
authors: Tinghan Ye, Shuaicheng Tong, Changkun Guan, Beste Basciftci, Pascal van Hentenryck
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sequential contextual stochastic programs model real-time decision systems in which each time epoch commits to an action under uncertainty whose consequences propagate into future decisions. In many practical contexts, these programs require obtaining solutions rapidly as new information becomes available. These problems can be represented through scenario approximations to be solved by off-the-shelf optimization solvers, which achieve high decision quality offline but typically run in seconds to minutes per instance, falling short of the sub-second responses that peak periods of planning require. This paper develops a learning-based optimization proxy: a scenario-embedded neural network trained offline on solver-generated labels, paired online with a decoder that enforces feasibility, replacing the per-epoch solve with a single forward pass. The framework is specialized to omnichannel order fulfillment, where each arriving order requires a sub-second assignment of products to distribution centers and carrier services under stochastic delivery times and future demand. A two-stage contextual stochastic program is introduced to formulate this problem, and its contextual sample average approximation (C-SAA) supplies the offline labels, while a composite training loss combines label imitation, a constraint-violation penalty, and self-supervised cost alignment. In a calibrated simulator built from JD.com transactional records, a detailed computational study is provided. The proxy reduces decision latency by roughly 2800x relative to the online finite-sample C-SAA reference and improves over it by 3.3% in realized fulfillment cost. Relative to established fulfillment policies, the proxy lowers total realized cost by at least 10.7% and roughly halves the late-delivery rate.
tldr: This paper develops a learning-based optimization proxy for sequential contextual stochastic programs, applied to omnichannel order fulfillment.
motivation: Sequential contextual stochastic programs require sub-second decisions in peak periods, but traditional solvers are too slow.
method: A scenario-embedded neural network is trained offline on solver-generated labels and paired with a decoder for feasibility; a composite loss combines label imitation, constraint-violation penalty, and self-supervised cost alignment.
result: The proxy reduces decision latency by ~2800x and improves realized fulfillment cost by 3.3% over the reference, and outperforms established policies by at least 10.7%.
conclusion: Learning-based optimization proxies can effectively replace online solvers for real-time decision-making under uncertainty.

title: Amalgam Approach To Compactness In (quasi-)Banach Function Spaces
authors: Ivan Kotal\'ik Dalimil Pe\v{s}a
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present amalgam-type characterisations of compactness in quasi-Banach function spaces. We further treat, in the same spirit, several related topics, namely convergence, (uniform) absolute continuity of the norm, and almost-compact embeddings. We also treat the case of rearrangement-invariant spaces and show that most of our conditions can be formulated in terms of the non-increasing rearrangement and the representation space.
tldr: This paper presents amalgam-type characterizations of compactness in quasi-Banach function spaces, focusing on functional analysis rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To provide compactness criteria in quasi-Banach function spaces using an amalgam approach, extending known results from Banach spaces.
method: The authors develop amalgam-type characterizations and apply them to convergence, absolute continuity of norm, and almost-compact embeddings, also treating rearrangement-invariant spaces.
result: They obtain conditions for compactness formulated in terms of non-increasing rearrangement and representation space.
conclusion: The amalgam approach yields a unified framework for compactness in quasi-Banach function spaces.

title: OAMP-Aided Joint Channel Estimation And Data Detection For Oddm Systems
authors: Kehan Huang, Min Qiu, Akram Shafie, Jinhong Yuan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, to address the challenge of joint channel estimation and data detection (JED) for orthogonal delay-Doppler (DD) division multiplexing (ODDM) in doubly selective channels, we propose an orthogonal approximate message passing (OAMP)-aided JED (OAMP-JED) receiver. We first formulate a bilinear cross-domain JED model, which can be linearized into separate channel estimation and data detection subproblems. The proposed OAMP-JED receiver alternately executes two OAMP modules for these subproblems, effectively coupled through a variational noise term to account for model uncertainty. Leveraging OAMP's error orthogonality, we derive closed-form scalar-variance updates to enable efficient and principled soft information exchange between the modules, thereby mitigating error propagation during JED. Simulation results show that, for both uncoded and coded ODDM, OAMP-JED achieves a lower bit error rate (BER) than benchmark schemes. Moreover, its BER performance closely approaches that of OAMP with perfect CSI.
tags: joint channel estimation and data detection
tldr: This paper proposes an OAMP-based receiver for joint channel estimation and data detection in ODDM systems, focusing on communication engineering rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Joint channel estimation and data detection in doubly selective channels is challenging for ODDM systems, and existing methods suffer from error propagation.
method: A bilinear cross-domain JED model is linearized into separate subproblems, and two OAMP modules are alternately executed with closed-form scalar-variance updates for soft information exchange.
result: The proposed OAMP-JED receiver achieves lower BER than benchmark schemes and approaches the performance of OAMP with perfect CSI.
conclusion: OAMP-JED effectively mitigates error propagation and provides efficient joint estimation and detection for ODDM systems.
keywords: joint channel estimation and data detection

title: Boundedness Of $p$-adic Hardy--Hilbert And Erd\'elyi--Kober Fractional Integral Operators On $p$-adic Ces\`aro Function Spaces
authors: Rishabh Saini, Qaiser Jahan, Salman Ashraf
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce Ces\`aro function spaces over [MATH]-adic fields and investigate their fundamental properties, such as the dilation operator and the Minkowski-type integral inequality. We establish boundedness result for [MATH]-adic Hardy--Hilbert-type integral operators acting on [MATH]-adic Ces\`aro function spaces, and as an application we derive [MATH]-adic analogue of the Hardy inequality, the Hilbert inequality, and the Hardy-Littlewood-P\'{o}lya inequality. Furthermore, we define the [MATH]-adic analogue of the Erd\'elyi--Kober fractional integral operators and prove their boundedness on [MATH]-adic Ces\`aro function spaces with the help of the obtained boundedness result.
tldr: This paper studies boundedness of p-adic Hardy-Hilbert and Erdélyi-Kober fractional integral operators on p-adic Cesàro function spaces, which is a topic in p-adic harmonic analysis and functional analysis.
motivation: To extend classical inequalities and operator theory to the p-adic setting, which has applications in number theory and p-adic analysis.
method: Introduces Cesàro function spaces over p-adic fields, studies their properties, and proves boundedness of integral operators using Minkowski-type inequalities.
result: Establishes boundedness results for p-adic Hardy-Hilbert-type operators and p-adic Erdélyi-Kober fractional integral operators on these spaces, deriving p-adic analogues of classical inequalities.
conclusion: The work contributes to p-adic analysis but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Abstract Orlicz-Morrey Spaces And Applications
authors: J. Zhou F. Shan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25455v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work introduces a class of abstract Orlicz-Morrey spaces endowed with a ball-basis on general measure spaces and defines the associated concept of \(\Psi\)-bounded oscillation operators. Within this framework, we establish pointwise estimates and norm inequalities for these operators via sparse domination techniques. As applications, we verify that this class of \(\Psi\)-bounded oscillation operators includes maximal operators and Carleson-type operators on general measure spaces, as well as \(\omega\)-Calder\'on-Zygmund operators and intrinsic square operators on \(^n\), thus providing a generalization of certain classical Orlicz-Morrey spaces and their associated operator theory.
tldr: This paper introduces abstract Orlicz-Morrey spaces and establishes norm inequalities for Ψ-bounded oscillation operators via sparse domination.
motivation: To generalize classical Orlicz-Morrey spaces and operator theory to general measure spaces.
method: Defines abstract Orlicz-Morrey spaces with a ball-basis and Ψ-bounded oscillation operators, then uses sparse domination techniques to derive pointwise estimates and norm inequalities.
result: The class of Ψ-bounded oscillation operators includes maximal operators, Carleson-type operators, ω-Calderón-Zygmund operators, and intrinsic square operators.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for operator theory on general measure spaces, extending classical results.

title: Kontsevich Graphs Associated With Specific Multiple Zeta Values
authors: Kota Baba
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The primary aim of this paper is to provide an explicit construction of Kontsevich graphs whose integrals give certain multiple zeta values.
